title: Streaming a PC to a Switch

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Nintendo Switch has a small screen and modest hardware. What if it were just the display for your gaming PC?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That sounds like a fun hack. Is that what Artemis-Switch does?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pretty much. It's Antoine's maintained fork of Moonlight-Switch, built for Apollo hosts, which are Sunshine-based. You stream a Windows or Linux PC, like Steam Big Picture or desktop apps, and the Switch decodes it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the PC does the heavy lifting.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. The Switch just decodes the stream in a Moonlight-compatible way. What Antoine adds is an overlay while you stream.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two menus. A Quick menu for host shortcuts, and a Performance menu with live bitrate and latency stats.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: C plus plus homebrew, in the devkitA64 and libnx lineage inherited from Moonlight-Switch. Pairing with an Apollo host happens over your local network.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is it only a fork, or did Antoine give anything back?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Both. The project page notes that the fork is separate from his merged toolchain fixes on upstream Moonlight-Switch, for newer devkitPro releases. It's licensed under GPL three.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The README covers build prerequisites, installing the dot N R O file, and pairing with your host.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And there's a blog post that goes through the screenshots and the two other homebrew projects.
